title: Thoughts on my game? It's a 1v1 fighting game where your webcam is the controller
author: Alchemist_humper69
selftext:
I've been building a game called **POWoww** and I'd really like some outside eyes on it before I keep going.

**What it is:** a 1v1 fighting game you play in a browser tab with your webcam. There's no controller and nothing to install. You stand up, you throw a punch, and your fighter in the 3D ring throws the same punch. Left/right punches, left/right kicks, and a block. Land hits, keep your guard up, drop the other person.

**The part I think is actually interesting:** it doesn't ship with one hardcoded idea of what a punch looks like. Before your first match you do a short calibration where you throw a few reps of each move at the camera, and it trains a small model on *your* movement right there in the tab. So it learns your jab, not the average of everyone else's. Pose tracking runs locally — the video never leaves your machine, only the detected move goes out.

Both players' moves go to one server that decides what actually landed, so nobody wins by lagging or by editing their client.

**Background / why:** I wanted a fighting game where the skill was physical instead of memorizing frame data, and I got annoyed that "motion controls" always means buying a peripheral. Webcams are already everywhere. Doing it in the browser means the whole ask is "click a link" — which matters a lot when the game is dead without a second person in the room. It's a solo project: design, 3D, netcode, the ML pipeline, all of it, so it's rough in the places you'd expect.

**Honest thoughts / where I'm stuck:**

* Calibration is the hardest sell. It's the very first thing you hit and it's the least fun part, and I've rewritten it several times. I don't know if it's still too long.
* Detection feel is a constant tradeoff — loosen it and you get phantom punches, tighten it and real punches get eaten.
* Kicks are much harder than punches, because a webcam usually can't see your legs.
* Multiplayer works but it's a one-person player base right now, which is its own problem for a fighting game.

**Stuff I'd love thoughts on:** does the pitch even make you want to try it? Would you stand up in front of your webcam to play something? How much setup would you sit through before quitting? And if you do try it, does your first punch register the way you expected?

Free, no ads, no paywall on matches — I don't want to gate the one thing that makes a fighting game work.

Link: [https://powoww.io](https://powoww.io/) — needs a webcam, and give it a minute on the first load

comments.author: blacklagoon25009
comments.body: It's a novel idea. I think people will want it local vs networked. You run into the same turnoff with MS kinect due to capturing. VR players are most likely to adopt something like this, people who have used a wii, ps move controllers.
